Subject: Vendor registration + invoice routing for Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks for the intro — we're ready to add Redwood Inference as a vendor in our payments portal so we can route POs and automate invoice payments. To get the enrollment queued, can you confirm the following items and share any AP onboarding packet you normally provide?

Quick list from our side:
- Legal company name and VAT/TIN used on invoices
- Bank details for EFT (routing/IBAN) or if you enable payment via our network (we support bank + virtual card)
- Whether Redwood requires PO numbers on invoices and what field you expect them in (invoice header vs line-level)
- Sample invoice or sample PO we can validate against our parser
- Any self-billing or tax-exempt arrangements we should know about

We typically require either a PDF invoice matching the PO or our portal-compatible XML for automatic matching. If you have a vendor AP packet, please attach.

Attaching: sample PO request template (we'll send your vendor record once we have the packet).

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 20-min call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Laura Simpson
Vendor Ops | GNS Payments

Laura — thanks for the clear checklist. I've attached our AP onboarding packet and a short routing spec. High level responses below; happy to jump on a call if you prefer.

Attachments: RNW_AP_Onboarding_Packet_v2.pdf (includes bank details, tax ids, remittance instructions, contact matrix)

Responses to your bullets:
- Legal name / VAT / TIN: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US EIN: 12-3456789). VAT: not applicable for the US-entity invoices; for EU customers we invoice Redwood Inference Ltd. (details in packet).
- Bank details: Included in the packet — we provide ACH (US) and SWIFT for wire. We also accept remittance via our payment partner network (we can accept virtual card if enabled on your portal).
- PO numbers: We require a PO number on the invoice header ("PO Number" field). For automatic reconciliation our parser maps it to header PO and also supports a line-level reference for split invoices; prefer header.
- Sample invoice: see sample in packet (page 3).
- Self-billing: We do not expect customers to self-bill by default. If GNS uses a self-bill arrangement, we need a signed self-bill agreement and confirmation of VAT treatment for EU invoices prior to enrollment.

A couple of clarifying questions for your team:
1) Does your portal support multiple remit destinations per vendor (we have separate remit for EU entities)?
2) Are there specific invoice filename conventions your parser requires (we usually send PDF named RNW_{invoice}_{YYYYMMDD}.pdf)

I'll loop in Karthik on VAT specifics if you need supporting documentation for EU entity setup.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — packet received and looks good. A couple follow-ups after our review: 

1) Portal remit destinations: we can support multiple remit accounts under one vendor record but each remit must be tied to a legal entity. We'll need the EU entity docs as part of onboarding if you want EU invoices routed to a different account.

2) Filename conventions: our parser is flexible; header PO detection prefers invoice header but we can map line-level fields in the portal config. Your RNW_{invoice}_{YYYYMMDD}.pdf is fine.

3) Self-bill: we will not enable self-billing without a signed agreement. For VAT validation on EU invoices, our tax-compliance team requires a VAT registration certificate and an EU invoice sample. Can your team provide "Redwood Inference Ltd." VAT cert and one EU invoice sample?

Attached: example parsed PO we used for testing (PO-12345-GNS.pdf).

We can enable a non-production vendor record for a smoke test once we have the EU docs and bank remits if you want to test a single invoice/PO match. Are you able to accept NET30 via ACH? If not, what are your preferred payment terms?

Best,
Laura
Vendor Ops | GNS Payments

[Attachment: PO-12345-GNS.pdf]

- PO acceptance: header PO preferred; we'll ensure our invoices include the header PO field exactly as you expect.
